problem.title: Clean Payer Names and Extract Contact Domains
problem.prompt: You are working with a prior authorization cycle time tracking system modeled on CMS Medicare & Medicaid datasets. The `payer_contacts` table stores contact information for insurance payers, but the `payer_name` column is inconsistently formatted with extra whitespace, mixed case, and unwanted suffixes like ' INC' or ' LLC'. The `contact_email` column contains valid email addresses. Write a query that cleans each payer name by trimming whitespace, capitalizing each word properly, removing the ' INC' and ' LLC' suffixes (case-insensitive), and extracts the domain portion (everything after the '@') from the contact email. Return the `payer_id`, the cleaned `payer_name_clean`, and the extracted `email_domain`, ordered by `payer_id`.

display.context: You are working with a prior authorization cycle time tracking system modeled on CMS Medicare & Medicaid datasets.
display.task: Write a query that cleans payer names by trimming whitespace, capitalizing words, removing company suffixes, and extracts email domains.

table_notes.payer_contacts: holds contact information for insurance payers with inconsistently formatted names and email addresses

output_field_notes.payer_id: the unique identifier for each payer
output_field_notes.payer_name_clean: the payer name after cleaning whitespace, capitalizing words, and removing INC or LLC suffixes
output_field_notes.email_domain: the domain portion of the contact email address after the at-sign

field_logic: payer_name_clean: take the payer_name, trim surrounding whitespace, capitalize the first letter of each word, then remove any trailing INC or LLC suffix regardless of case
email_domain: take the contact_email and extract everything that comes after the at-sign
edge_cases: If a payer name has extra spaces around it, remove them before cleaning.
If a payer name ends with INC or LLC in any mix of upper and lower case, strip that suffix.
If the contact email has a subdomain, include the entire domain after the at-sign.
display.filter_note: All rows from the payer_contacts table are included.
display.order_by_note: Results are ordered by payer_id in ascending order.

problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE payer_contacts (payer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, payer_name VARCHAR(200), contact_email VARCHAR(200), state_code CHAR(2));
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO payer_contacts (payer_id, payer_name, contact_email, state_code) VALUES (1, '  anthem blue cross llc  ', 'claims@anthem.com', 'CA'), (2, 'united healthcare INC', 'pa.team@uhc.com', 'NY'), (3, 'aetna', 'auth@aetna.healthcare.com', 'CT'), (4, 'CIGNA HEALTH inc', 'review@cigna.com', 'PA'), (5, '  humana  LLC  ', 'prior.auth@humana.net', 'FL'), (6, 'Blue Shield california', 'contact@blueshieldca.org', 'CA');
problem.test_data: INSERT INTO payer_contacts (payer_id, payer_name, contact_email, state_code) VALUES (101, 'kaiser permanente', 'auth@kp.org', 'CA'), (102, '  molina healthcare LLC  ', 'pa@molina.com', 'TX'), (103, 'CENTENE CORP INC', 'review@centene.com', 'MO'), (104, '  wellcare health plans inc  ', 'claims@wellcare.net', 'FL'), (105, 'carefirst bluecross blueshield llc', 'prior.auth@carefirst.com', 'MD'), (106, 'OSCAR health INC', 'team@oscar.com', 'NY'), (107, '  independence blue cross  ', 'auth@ibx.com', 'PA'), (108, 'harvard pilgrim health care Inc', 'pa@hphc.org', 'MA'), (109, 'TUFTS HEALTH PLAN llc', 'review@tuftshealthplan.com', 'MA'), (110, '  emblemhealth INC  ', 'contact@emblemhealth.com', 'NY'), (111, 'highmark inc', 'claims@highmark.com', 'PA'), (112, '  premera blue cross LLC  ', 'auth@premera.com', 'WA'), (113, 'HEALTHFIRST inc', 'pa@healthfirst.org', 'NY'), (114, 'horizon blue cross blue shield', 'review@horizon.com', 'NJ'), (115, '  regence bluecross blueshield llc  ', 'prior.auth@regence.com', 'OR');
hints: You'll need to chain multiple text functions to clean the payer name: start by removing extra whitespace, then fix capitalization, then strip unwanted endings.
Use INITCAP to capitalize each word after trimming. Then use REGEXP_REPLACE with a case-insensitive pattern to remove ' INC' or ' LLC' from the end of the string.
For the email domain, SPLIT_PART can break the email at the '@' character and take the second part. Combine TRIM, INITCAP, REGEXP_REPLACE for the name; use SPLIT_PART for the domain.
problem.answer_key: SELECT payer_id, REGEXP_REPLACE(INITCAP(TRIM(payer_name)), ' (inc|llc)$', '', 'i') AS payer_name_clean, SPLIT_PART(contact_email, '@', 2) AS email_domain FROM payer_contacts ORDER BY payer_id;

_meta.scenario: a prior authorization cycle time tracking system across payers

user_solution:
/* notes */

SELECT
    payer_id,
    REGEXP_REPLACE(INITCAP(TRIM(payer_name)), ' (inc|llc)$', '', 'gi') AS payer_name_clean,
    SPLIT_PART(TRIM(contact_email), '@', 2) AS email_domain
FROM payer_contacts
ORDER BY payer_id;
